message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to call out my coworker Jackson for lying about his boxing and martial arts skills. Let me start by understanding the situation better. Jackson works with me, and he's always bragging about how he was a top-notch boxer with a 23-0 record, supposedly one of the best in the valley. He also talks about how he could kick anyone's ass and how he's still in great shape despite being out of his prime. But I know for a fact that most of this is just bull. If he was really that good, there should be some records or mentions online, right? I tried Googling his name, and nothing came up. So, I'm pretty sure he's lying about his boxing achievements. On the other hand, I'm 19 and have been training in Muay Thai for eight years. I also wrestled in high school and am very fit. I'm proud of my progress in martial arts and fitness, especially since I used to be overweight. I rarely hang out with Jackson outside of work because he never stops talking about his lies, like how he could have graduated culinary school with high honors but got kicked out for fighting, or how he knows high-profile gangbangers who make millions a year, which is why he works in this restaurant just for fun, not because he needs the money. But last weekend, we ended up hanging out, having a few beers, and watching UFC. During the Blagoy Ivanov vs. Taimur Iasaf fight, Jackson said, "I could KO both these bums, no challenge." That's when I snapped and told him I doubted he could even kick my ass, especially since I'm 19 and half his weight. I also called him out on his boxing bullshit and mentioned that nothing shows up when I Google his name. I challenged him to come down to my Muay Thai gym and try, saying I would "maul" him. He got all pissy and walked out, and then I told some of the coworkers I like about it. Most of them think I'm an asshole, although a few agreed with me. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong for me to call out Jackson like that? Let's break this down. First, I need to consider the context. We were hanging out, having beers, so it was a casual setting. But Jackson's constant lying about his skills and achievements is bothering me. I feel like he's not only exaggerating but also belittling my own achievements by constantly talking about his supposed superiority. When I called him out, I was standing up for myself and my skills. I was tired of him making false claims and wanted to set the record straight. However, the way I did it might have been confrontational and could have led to tension in the workplace. I also need to think about the consequences of my actions. By calling him out in front of others and then telling some coworkers about it, I might have damaged our working relationship. Most of my coworkers think I'm an asshole for doing this, which suggests that they either don't see the issue with Jackson's behavior or they think I overreacted. On the other hand, a few coworkers agreed with me, which means there might be some support for standing up to Jackson's lies. But overall, the majority think I was wrong to do it. I also need to consider Jackson's perspective. Maybe he feels insecure or is trying to compensate for something by lying about his skills. Or perhaps he genuinely believes in his abilities, even if there's no evidence to back it up. Either way, calling him out publicly might have hurt his feelings or made him feel embarrassed. Another thing to think about is the impact on our workplace. If I continue to confront Jackson like this, it could create a hostile work environment. It's important to maintain a professional relationship, even if I don't personally like him. I also wonder if there's a better way to handle this situation. Instead of calling him out in front of others, maybe I could have talked to him privately about his claims. That way, I could express my concerns without making him feel attacked or embarrassed. Additionally, I should reflect on why I feel the need to challenge his claims. Is it because I'm insecure about my own skills? Or is it because I genuinely believe he's spreading misinformation? Understanding my own motivations can help me decide whether my actions were justified. In summary, while I feel like I was standing up for myself and my skills by calling out Jackson's lies, the way I did it might have been confrontational and could have negative consequences in the workplace. It's important to consider the impact of my actions on my relationships with coworkers and the overall work environment.
